topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, lecturer background, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental debate and evidence regarding whether cancer development is driven primarily by intrinsic cellular errors, inherited genetic risk, or external environmental exposures.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Causes of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, focusing on the discovery and multi-step mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mechanisms of DNA Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage through bulky adducts and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Microenvironment, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish direct mutational initiation from non-mutagenic tumor promotion and explain how tissue microenvironments and developmental life stages affect susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic and evaluate their associated risks.
